class.name: PSX
class.brief_description: Script access to the PS1 renderer: switch it on and off, override its settings while the game runs, and read its statistics.
class.description:
The PS1 renderer is installed by [member ProjectSettings.rendering/psx/enabled] (a restart is needed). Once installed, its live settings are resolved for each viewport every frame, a later source overriding an earlier one: 1. The project settings ([code]rendering/psx/*[/code]). 2. The [PSXSettings] node in the scene the viewport shows. 3. Overrides set through this singleton with [method set_setting]. A [PSXMaterial3D] can then turn dithering on or off and subdivision off for its own surfaces. The setting names are [code]"active"[/code], [code]"dither"[/code], [code]"lighting_mode"[/code], [code]"default_ambient"[/code], [code]"world_scale"[/code], [code]"subdivide_size"[/code], [code]"texture_max_size"[/code], [code]"texture_depth"[/code] and [code]"texture_max_colors"[/code] (see [method get_setting_names]). The first four cost nothing to change. Changing the others makes the next frame convert the meshes or textures it draws again, a one-frame hitch. Resolution, VRAM scale and texture banks are not here: they need a restart. [codeblock] # A graphics menu: PS1 look on or off, dithering on or off. func _on_ps1_look_toggled(on): PSX.set_active(on)
func _on_dither_toggled(on): PSX.set_setting("dither", on) [/codeblock] Overrides set here last until they are cleared with [method clear_setting] or [method clear_settings], or the game quits. They are not saved.

method.name: clear_setting
method.description: Removes the script override of the setting [param name], so the scene's [PSXSettings] node or the project setting applies again.

method.name: clear_settings
method.description: Removes every script override, including the one [method set_active] makes.

method.name: get_setting
method.description: Returns the value of the setting [param name] from the project settings and the script overrides. A [PSXSettings] node's overrides apply only to the viewports showing its world, so they are not included; use [method PSXSettings.get_value] for those.

method.name: get_setting_names
method.description: Returns the names [method set_setting] and [method get_setting] accept.

method.name: get_stats
method.description: Returns statistics for the last frame the PS1 renderer handled, from the viewport drawn last: - [code]frame[/code]: the PS1 renderer's frame counter. - [code]active[/code]: [code]false[/code] when the PS1 view was off and Godot's renderer drew the frame (the other entries are then 0). - [code]instances[/code]: objects drawn. - [code]triangles_in[/code] and [code]triangles_drawn[/code]: triangles sent to the GTE, and drawn after culling. - [code]conversions[/code]: meshes and textures converted this frame. - [code]textures_resident[/code], [code]textures_baked[/code]: textures in texture memory, and how many of them came from a [PSXTexture]. - [code]texture_fallbacks[/code]: surfaces drawn untextured because texture memory was full. - [code]texture_banks[/code], [code]vram_free_percent[/code]: texture memory in use. - [code]raster_usec[/code]: time spent drawing the frame, in microseconds.

method.name: is_active
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the PS1 view is on, from the project setting and the script override. See [method set_active].

method.name: is_available
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the PS1 renderer is installed: [member ProjectSettings.rendering/psx/enabled] was on at startup and the rendering method is Forward+ or Mobile.

method.name: set_active
method.description: Switches the PS1 view on or off for every viewport. When off, Godot's own renderer draws the 3D, at the window's resolution. Same as [code]set_setting("active", active)[/code].

method.name: set_setting
method.description: Overrides the setting [param name] for every viewport, over the project settings and [PSXSettings] nodes. [param value] is converted to the setting's type and clamped to its range.
